title: Pocketwire Advance Servicing Standard — Grace Period and Past-Due Status
content:
**Standard 1. Past-due status.** A Pocketwire Advance still not fully repaid when the tier's grace period in calendar days has passed after its due date makes the line past due, and the line's past-due-since date records that day. When the line becomes past due its consecutive on-time repayments go back to 0.

**Standard 2. Extended advances.** No late fee is booked on an advance that was extended while the extension's new due date and grace period have not passed.

**Standard 3. Retired clause.** The following clause is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current Pocketwire Advance basis for assessing late fees:

> *No longer in force:* "For each full late-fee period after the grace period ends, a late fee is booked on the advance at its unpaid principal times the weekly late-fee percentage, rounded to the cent (half up) and raised to the minimum late fee, numbered by period; late fees stop once their total on the advance would exceed the late fee cap of its principal, the last one being cut to the cap."

## Standard 1 on a timeline (hypothetical)

A line on Pocketwire Advance Standard, grace period 7 calendar days, has an advance due on the 10th of a month.

| Day | Advance still not fully repaid | Line |
|---|---|---|
| 10th (due date) | Yes | Active |
| 16th | Yes | Active — 7 calendar days have not yet passed |
| 17th | Yes | Past due; the past-due-since date is the 17th |

Had the advance been repaid in full on the 16th, the grace period would have passed with nothing unpaid and Standard 1 would not make the line past due.

## Standard 2 in brief

An advance whose due date was extended is measured from the new due date: until that new due date and the grace period after it have passed, no late fee is booked on it.
